issue.description:
Found while landing irrevers-92e6e55c's chain: with the policy-lock warning
removed, a guarded hook invocation on an instrumented host still emits, every
single call:

    icg_health_event event=run_started run_id=run-1788832822274336572-1548580

`HealthStore::start_run` (src/health.rs:1077) prints it unconditionally after
persisting the lifecycle marker.

## Why it is the same problem as the parent, with a different cause

irrevers-92e6e55c is about a warning the guard cannot avoid emitting because
it asks for a lock it can never hold. This one is a line the guard chooses to
emit on a healthy, entirely uneventful path. Both land on stderr, which is
the channel a real fault has to announce itself on: on lab that is 48 agents,
on ex44 79, one line per tool call each. The cache-ownership bug
(irrevers-63087cdd) announced itself as a stderr warning and was found only
because the stream was otherwise quiet.

The neighbouring emitters are not the same and should stay:
`event=crash_detected`, `crash_recorded`, `run_started`'s sibling
`*_failed` variants (health.rs:814, 1173; main.rs:953, 1143, 1259, 1275,
1279, 1365, 1397) all report an actual fault or a recovered crash.
`run_started` is the only one that fires when nothing has happened.

## Also blocks a stronger regression test

`hook_invocation_leaves_administrator_owned_policy_untouched`
(tests/fail_closed_runtime_tests.rs) wanted to assert stderr is empty after a
guarded call. It currently filters `icg_health_event ` lines out before
asserting, with a comment pointing here. When this is fixed, that filter
should be deleted and the assertion restored to plain emptiness.

## Options, not yet decided

- Drop the print. The run id is already persisted in the health store and is
  recoverable from there; nothing consumes the stderr line.
- Or gate it behind an opt-in (ICG_DEBUG / a verbosity flag), so the
  lifecycle trace stays available when someone is actually debugging one.

The second keeps the diagnostic; the first is what the deployed hosts need.
Prefer the second only if something demonstrably reads these lines today --
check before assuming.

## Done when
- A guarded hook invocation on a healthy host emits nothing on stderr.
- Fault and crash-recovery events still print, with tests proving it.
- The filter in hook_invocation_leaves_administrator_owned_policy_untouched
  is removed and the assertion is `stderr.is_empty()` again.

issue.close_reason: Research completed. Hypothesis refuted: neither Claude Code nor Codex CLI provides fail-closed hook timeout/error behavior by default. Claude Code fails-open on timeout and most errors (only exit 2 blocks). Codex CLI fails-open on timeout by default (requires opt-in ). Implication:  cannot rely on harness-native behavior for fail-closed enforcement; must accept standing-daemon watchdog cost or re-scope to PATH-wrapper approach.
issue.description: plan.md Architecture lines 73-87 makes this a hard precondition of irrevers-cd3f4c44: 'fail closed when the process is dead' needs something to notice the process is gone, and a standing watchdog is the guard-as-daemon architecture ideation explicitly killed (Lens-1 idea #69). Leading hypothesis, NOT yet confirmed: if Claude Code's and Codex's own PreToolUse hook systems already have configurable behavior for 'the hook command errored, timed out, or never responded', then fail-closed means configuring THAT harness setting once reliability is validated, not building new standing infrastructure. DO THIS FIRST, before assuming a watchdog is needed. If neither harness supports it, cd3f4c44 must either accept the standing-daemon cost or be re-scoped. Was recorded only as prose inside the genesis bead, which declined to track it -- inconsistent with irrevers-0c6358a4, an identical research gate that does have a bead. Plan: docs/plan/plan.md Architecture 'Open implementation question'.
issue.notes:
## Research findings (2026-08-15)

### Claude Code hook behavior
- Timeout on command/http/mcp_tool hooks: **FAILS-OPEN** (call continues)
- Only Agent SDK callback hooks block on timeout
- Exit code 2: **FAILS-CLOSED** (blocks call)
- All other exit codes: **FAILS-OPEN** (non-blocking, continues)
- HTTP errors / connection failures: **FAILS-OPEN**

### Codex CLI hook behavior  
- Timeout: **FAILS-OPEN by default** (allowed-but-flagged-ungoverned mode)
- Fail-closed requires opt-in: `echo closed > ~/.acp/failmode`
- Exit 2: **FAILS-CLOSED**
- Other failures: can deny, but `PREMPTI_FAIL_OPEN=1` overrides

### Hypothesis status: **REFUTED**

Neither harness provides fail-closed behavior on hook timeout/error by default. Codex requires opt-in configuration; Claude Code fails-open on all error conditions except exit 2.

### Implication for `irrevers-cd3f4c44`
The graduated fail-open→fail-closed policy CANNOT rely on harness-native hook behavior. `irrevers-cd3f4c44` must either:
1. Accept standing-daemon cost for a watchdog process, OR
2. Re-scope to use PATH-wrapper binary as fail-closed enforcement layer (no daemon needed)

Sources:
- Claude Code: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks (Timeouts, Exit codes sections)
- Codex: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks + web search
issue.title: Verify Claude Code and Codex hook-error/timeout configuration can substitute for a watchdog

issue.description:
Installing icg on a machine that also builds it makes `cargo test` corrupt
the live denial log.

## Observed

ex44 was instrumented in practice mode on 2026-09-06. By 2026-09-07, 14 of
its 72 denial records named patterns that exist in no shipped pack:

    vault-kv-destroy            4
    kubectl-delete-pvc          3
    deny-reset                  2
    guard-crash                 2
    kubectl-delete-deployment   1
    api-key-in-write            1
    test-dangerous              1

Those are test-fixture pattern ids -- `kubectl-delete-*` from
tests/fixtures/developer-scenarios/debugging-false-positives-*.json,
`vault-kv-destroy` from the fictional pack the docs used to describe.

## Cause

`DenialStore` falls back to /var/cache/icg/denials.jsonl when ICG_DENIAL_LOG
is unset. Before the install that path did not exist, so test writes went
nowhere and nobody noticed. Now it exists and is agent-writable by design,
so every `cargo test` that exercises a deny path appends to the same file the
practice trial is collecting into.

lab is unaffected: it does not build the project. Only a host that is both
instrumented and a dev box is exposed -- which is exactly ex44.

## Impact

ex44's practice-trial data is not trustworthy and cannot simply be filtered
after the fact with confidence: a fixture id is identifiable, but a fixture
exercising a REAL pattern id is not distinguishable from live traffic.

## Done when

## Genesis Bead
Tied to plan: docs/plan/plan.md

## Overview
A guard for AI coding/automation agents (Claude Code and Codex CLI) that intercepts commands before execution and blocks or redirects irreversible operations, extending -- and eventually superseding most of -- the existing org-rule-guard.py PreToolUse hook. Two front-ends (a PATH-wrapper binary and native PreToolUse hook adapters) share one engine and a modular pack-per-tool rule set.

## Source of truth for scope
DO NOT read a bead-ID checklist here. Two previous genesis bodies were retired precisely because their hardcoded ID lists went stale, and bead-rs cannot edit a description to repair one. The live blocker list IS the phase list:

    bead why --id <this-bead-id>      # every open bead blocking completion
    bead list --ready                 # what is actually startable right now

## Progress
- [ ] Phase 0 -- deploy path: icg-ci pipeline (DONE), trust pointer (DONE), self-updater (DONE, but see deferral 7), release-integrity Layers 1/2/4, release-cutting runbook, and the deploy-location decision
- [ ] Phase 1 -- Tier 1 rules, deny-only, both front-ends where applicable
- [ ] Phase 2 -- cross-invocation state (Tier 2)
- [ ] Phase 3 -- redirect-mechanism richness (updatedInput, additionalContext, value derivation)
- [ ] Phase 4 -- ideation run 1 finalists
- [ ] Phase 5 -- ideation run 2 finalists

## Deliberate deferrals and known-accepted gaps (the fallback role of this bead)
Recorded so a later reader does not re-litigate them. A three-round /plan-to-bead audit decided NOT to fix these:
1. STALE PROSE INSIDE BEAD DESCRIPTIONS. bead-rs cannot edit a description and its --notes field has no read path, so the only way to fix a sentence is to close and recreate the bead. That was judged not worth the churn for the following, all of which are prose-only -- WHERE PROSE AND EDGES DISAGREE, TRUST THE EDGES:
   - ~8 open beads cite dead short-form icg-* IDs (provenance references from before the bead-rs rehydration).
   - Two beads contain unresolvable positional placeholders from a bf batch file: the Layer 2 review bead's 'bead @2' means the coverage-diff report bead, and the admin-dispatch bead's '@1' means the self-updater bead.
   - The Codex compatibility-matrix bead attributes itself to ideation run 2; it is run 1 finalist #6. plan.md has it right (Phase 4).
   - The wrapper additionalContext bead says 'no current bead depends on this specifically' -- the Codex-fallback bead now does.
   - The stale-HEAD push bead calls itself an exception to a 'no-I/O' engine constraint. The plan's constraint is zero-NETWORK-I/O; local filesystem reads were never exceptions. Do not generalize that bead's wording to the beads pack's stat check.
   - The test-infrastructure bead's stated symptom ('cannot find module icg::coverage') is stale -- src/lib.rs is committed and exports it.
2. REDUNDANT EDGES. ~50 blocker edges are transitively implied by another edge on the same bead. Left as documentary; they inflate apparent fan-in for critical-path analysis.
3. VALUE-DERIVATION HELPERS keeps its plural title, matching plan.md's own component name, despite failing a strict single-task title test.
4. CRATES.IO as a secondary version-check signal is named in the plan but has no bead -- conditional on ever publishing the crate.
5. ORG-RULE-GUARD.PY RULES 1 AND 2 (.github/workflows, kind: Job/CronJob) are not excluded on principle but are not scheduled by any phase, so the realistic end state is a kubectl-only rump PLUS those two. Rule 4 (mutating kubectl) is excluded permanently. Rule 5 is only half-absorbed: Phase 1 takes the Bash channel, the Write/Edit half stays.
6. TWO BEADS LOOK ALREADY SATISFIED by committed work (test-infrastructure setup, coverage-diff fixtures) but stay open: the fixtures encode the very schema naming the reconciliation bead is chartered to decide, so closing them now would ratify the un-reconciled shape. Run the test suite and close them once that decision lands.
7. TWO PHASE 0 ARTIFACTS SHIPPED INTO AGENT-WRITABLE PATHS and their beads are closed as complete -- the self-updater closed while the deploy-location decision governing its path was still open. Rather than reopen completed work, the residual is tracked as its own migration bead. Phase 0 is load-bearing: per plan.md nothing in later phases is meaningfully tamper-resistant until the deploy-location and release-gating work lands.

Practice mode first, on lab (48 agent processes) rather than ex44 (79).
Non-enforcing by construction: `icg hook --practice` allows every call and

Baseline from replaying 20,007 real agent commands: 99.80% allow, 0.205%
deny, and seven of ten packs never fired — including every fleet-specific
rule (needle-cleanup, bare-nato-session, beads-shared-checkout-write,
deprecated-bead-cli).

## Done when
- install.sh run on lab with --hook and the practice flag set
- `icg coverage --list` on lab loads 10 packs
- the agent identity can write the telemetry cache (verified, not assumed)
- a week of `icg status --denials --pattern-summary` collected
- the would-deny list contains nothing the fleet legitimately needed

by the 2.6% of commands whose heredoc bodies contain an apostrophe, and the

  curl -fsSL .../install.sh | sudo bash -s -- \
    --version v0.1.3 --practice --hook --agent-user coding

bypass (irrevers-e8359267), so a practice week on it would have been blind to

- enforcing path: deny -- the guard is capable of blocking if promoted
- heredoc+apostrophe: deny -- the bypass is closed on the deployed binary

Also verified before deploying that the hook cannot break a tool call: packs
missing, packs unreadable, corrupt pack JSON, unwritable cache, empty stdin,
malformed stdin, unknown tool -- every case returns valid JSON, allow,
exit 0, in BOTH practice and enforcing modes.

In a fresh shell with no recorded pull, the first command above returns permissionDecision deny with the flush-before-pull reason; after `git pull` has been observed through the hook, the same command returns allow. Split child of irrevers-8d1f79a7 (auto-split). Covers the parent's third acceptance criterion.

The ownership table in docs/operators/deployment-guide.md (~lines 101-112) currently lists /etc/icg/ artifacts but omits the fail-closed policy state and its lock entirely. Add them and make the ownership model explicit.

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] The ownership table gains rows for /etc/icg/fail-closed-policy.json and its .lock, both stated as root-only (root:root, not writable by the guarded-agent user).
- [ ] The guide states explicitly that guarded agents neither write nor lock the policy file or its lock -- they consume an already-committed policy decision read-only.
- [ ] The guide explains why the 'agent-writable .lock' alternative was rejected: an agent must not hold a lock on state it cannot legitimately alter, and even with the lock held the subsequent policy write would fail on the root-only file. Rejected, not deferred.
- [ ] Wording matches the surrounding table/guide style and the comments already in src/fail_closed.rs (reconcile_release_health's doc comment) and src/main.rs (the 'guarded process never reconciles' notes).
- [ ] No policy value or credential appears in the doc; references and paths only.

issue.description:
## Genesis Bead
Tied to plan: docs/plan/plan.md

## Overview
A guard for AI coding/automation agents (Claude Code and Codex CLI) that intercepts commands before execution and blocks or redirects irreversible operations, extending -- and eventually superseding most of -- the existing org-rule-guard.py PreToolUse hook. Two front-ends (a PATH-wrapper binary and native PreToolUse hook adapters) share one engine and a modular pack-per-tool rule set.

## Source of truth for scope
DO NOT read a bead-ID checklist here -- the previous genesis bead was closed precisely because its hardcoded ID list went stale twice (once at the bead-rs rehydration, once at a decomposition split) and bead-rs cannot edit a description to repair it. The live blocker list IS the phase list:

    bead why --id <this-bead-id>      # every open bead blocking completion
    bead list --ready                 # what is actually startable right now

## Progress
- [ ] Phase 0 -- deploy path: icg-ci pipeline (DONE, closed), release-integrity Layers 1/2/4, self-updater, trust pointer (DONE, closed), release-cutting runbook, and the deploy-location requirement
- [ ] Phase 1 -- Tier 1 rules, deny-only, both front-ends where applicable
- [ ] Phase 2 -- cross-invocation state (Tier 2)
- [ ] Phase 3 -- redirect-mechanism richness (updatedInput, additionalContext, value derivation)
- [ ] Phase 4 -- ideation run 1 finalists
- [ ] Phase 5 -- ideation run 2 finalists

## Deliberate deferrals and known-accepted gaps (the fallback role of this bead)
Recorded here because a /plan-to-bead audit decided NOT to fix them, so a later reader does not re-litigate:
1. LEGACY IDs IN BEAD PROSE. Roughly ten open beads still cite dead short-form icg-* IDs in their descriptions (provenance references only). bead-rs cannot edit a description, and recreating ten beads to fix prose was judged worse than leaving it. Trust edges, not prose, when they disagree.
2. REDUNDANT EDGES. ~50 blocker edges are transitively implied by another edge on the same bead. Left in place as documentary; they inflate apparent fan-in if the graph is ever used for critical-path analysis.
3. VALUE-DERIVATION HELPERS keeps its plural title, matching plan.md's own component name, despite failing a strict single-task title test.
4. CRATES.IO as a secondary version-check signal is named in the plan but has no bead -- it is conditional on ever publishing the crate.
5. ORG-RULE-GUARD.PY RULES 1 AND 2 (.github/workflows, kind: Job/CronJob) are not excluded on principle but are not scheduled by any phase, so the realistic end state is a kubectl-only rump PLUS those two, not kubectl-only. Rule 4 (mutating kubectl) is permanently excluded.
6. TWO BEADS LOOK ALREADY SATISFIED by in-flight uncommitted work (test-infrastructure setup and coverage-diff fixtures) but stay open deliberately: the fixtures encode the very schema naming the naming-reconciliation bead is chartered to decide, so closing them now would lock in the un-reconciled shape.
7. PHASE 0 IS LOAD-BEARING. Per plan.md, nothing in later phases is meaningfully tamper-resistant until the deploy-location and release-gating work lands. Two Phase 0 artifacts have ALREADY shipped into agent-writable paths -- see the deploy-location bead, which is why it exists.

issue.description:
## Alternative for: Starvation alert: beads invisible in 
Original bead: irrevers-9c67e1b1

Run only if the adjudication pass finds a non-empty invisible bucket — otherwise record 'nothing to unstick' and finish. For each bead in that list, reconcile it against the predicates of bead-rs's actual ready query (visible via `bead list --ready --verbose`: base_status='open', manual_blocked unset, assignee IS NULL, no 'blocks' dependency on a non-closed issue, and no resource_locks row held by another issue under a live lease): (1) assignee or claim_epoch residue from a worker that is gone — clear it with `bead update <id> --clear-assignee`; `bead release <id>` only for in_progress beads, it refuses assigned-but-open ones; (2) a resource lock or lease held by an issue that is closed or whose fence has expired — recover with `bead doctor --starvation-recovery` (the supported repair; use `--starvation-check` output to confirm what it will change, and `bead doctor --rehearse` if uncertain); (3) an exclusion label from DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_LABELS (deferred/human/blocked) — remove it ONLY where the label's own record shows the fence has lapsed (a deferral or quarantine whose recorded revisit/expiry timestamp has passed); an active fence is never cleared automatically — instead comment on the bead that it is fenced by policy and leave it. Re-run `bead list --ready` after each fix and require the bead to appear in the frontier; record before/after state per bead via `bead update --notes`. Constraints: repair exclusively through the bead CLI — no direct SQL against beads.db, no hand-edits under .beads/, no in-repo diagnostic tooling (removed from this repo 2026-09-06 because hand-written SQL ignored resource_locks, leases and claim_epoch and could clear a live worker's claim).

Deploy location decision clarified in plan.md

Decided that guard artifacts should be deployed to root-owned system paths:
- Binary: /usr/local/bin/icg (root:root, 0755)
- Rule packs: /etc/icg/packs/ directory (root:root, 0755) with individual pack files (root:root, 0644) - MODULAR approach preferred

issue.description:
Split out of irrevers-e8359267, which fixed heredoc bodies.

`lex_shell_commands` does not parse `$( ... )` as a nested context. In

    git commit -q -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
    ... body containing "quotes" ...
    EOF
    )"

the first double quote inside the body closes the outer double-quoted word,
so the segment handed to the rules is truncated (506 of ~1200 characters in
the observed case) and lexing resumes mid-message.

## Not a bypass, and not a false positive

Verified after the heredoc fix:

- prose inside the message naming a destructive command -> allow (correct)
- a real destructive command after such a commit      -> deny  (correct)

The lexer recovers at the next newline, so trailing commands are still seen.

## What it does cost

`git-commit-without-pathspec` cannot match, because its regex is anchored
and the segment is a fragment. That is the residual ~129 of 476 `git commit`
invocations still missed after the message-pattern fix (irrevers-9ef830ec)
raised the catch rate 35 -> 106.

## Done when

- The lexer treats `$( ... )` as a nested command context with its own quote
  state, or the rule stops depending on seeing a complete invocation.
- `a_requoted_commit_message_still_reaches_the_pathspec_rule` in
  tests/heredoc_lexing_tests.rs is un-ignored and passes.
- The 20k-command corpus replay shows no new false positives.
issue.title: Lexer does not recurse into $( ) so a message containing a double quote truncates the segment

issue.description:
Found by irrevers-10fa65df while grep-verifying the lock ownership model for irrevers-8d1f79a7 criterion 2: locking must live only in operator / deployment-controller commands.

Reachability chain (all line numbers as of main 08f5be4):
  icg hook                 src/main.rs:1627  Commands::Hook
  shadowed tool (argv[0])  src/main.rs:1370 -> run_shadowed_tool -> src/main.rs:1177
  icg wrapper              src/main.rs:1807 -> run_shadowed_tool -> src/main.rs:1177
    -> recovered_guard_crash_requires_halt (src/main.rs:906)
    -> policy_store.record_poison_pill (src/main.rs:916)
    -> PolicyStore::record_poison_pill (src/fail_closed.rs:696)
    -> PolicyStore::update (src/fail_closed.rs:685)
    -> acquire_lock (src/fail_closed.rs:563)

This contradicts the documented invariant on acquire_lock (src/fail_closed.rs:557-562): 'Callers are therefore operator or deployment-controller actions, never a hook or wrapper invocation.' The fire condition is a recovered guard crash (health lifecycle startup_crash), i.e. exactly the degraded moment the guard least needs extra work in the guarded process.

Two failure shapes depending on layout:
1. Hardened layout (per irrevers-8d1f79a7: /etc/icg and its .lock root-only, guarded agent cannot write): acquire_lock fails with permission denied on open of fail-closed-policy.json.lock. The error is swallowed into a stderr warning (src/main.rs:920-922), so the poison-pill policy event the crash-recovery boundary exists to record is silently dropped - qualification is not reset exactly when a crash was just consumed. tests/fail_closed_runtime_tests.rs:126 (recovered_guard_crash_is_fail_open_by_default_and_persisted) asserts last_poison_pill_event.is_some() and only passes because the test's policy path is agent-writable; the asserted contract does not hold on the hardened layout the ownership model describes.
2. Non-hardened layout (agent-writable policy dir): a guarded tool call successfully takes the exclusive policy lock and mutates durable policy state - a hook performing a policy write and holding the operator lock, contending with icg policy reconcile.

Suggested direction (for whoever picks this up, not fixed here): route the crash-recovery poison-pill record through an operator/deployment-controller path (or persist it to a store the guarded agent legitimately owns, e.g. the health/state store, and let reconcile consume it), keeping PolicyStore writes behind the operator boundary. Also decide whether the runtime test should assert the hardened-layout behavior (event dropped + warning, no guarded write) instead of persistence.

Not fixed inside irrevers-10fa65df per its acceptance criterion 4.

## Resolution

Root Cause: Dependency deadlock created by Unravel blocking pattern.

Analysis:
- Original starvation alert irrevers-95014db4 (OPEN) was blocked by Unravel alternative irrevers-18ebf6e0
- Unravel alternative was IN_PROGRESS (assigned to worker icg47)
- This created a deadlock where:
  - Original bead could not enter ready frontier (blocked by IN_PROGRESS bead)
  - Blocking bead could not be claimed (already IN_PROGRESS)

Result:
- Ready frontier now shows 1 bead: irrevers-95014db4
- Starvation resolved

Recommendation: Unravel blocking pattern should mark original beads as deferred rather than creating blocking dependencies to prevent this deadlock pattern.

issue.description:
Split child of irrevers-beee1069 (argo-guarded-builder ships /etc/icg world-writable).

Root cause, confirmed: this image is built by kaniko, whose build umask is 0000,
so every directory a RUN created without an explicit mode shipped at 0777 in
0.1.0 — /etc/icg, /etc/icg/overrides, /var/cache/icg (and /root/.cargo).
/etc/icg/packs only escaped because the later `COPY packs /etc/icg/packs/`
imposed the source directory's mode on it. That is what makes
verify_artifact_directory_security (src/trust_pointer.rs) report "mode 40777"
on every hook invocation: anything in a guarded CI pod can rewrite
/etc/icg/trust-pointer.json and /etc/icg/packs and choose its own rules.

Scope: containers/argo-guarded-builder/Dockerfile only.

NOTE: a partial diff for this already exists uncommitted in the working tree
of ~/irreversible-command-gate from the failed attempts on the parent. Review,
verify and finish it rather than restarting from scratch.

Acceptance criteria:
- The mkdir RUN explicitly chowns root:root and chmods 0755 /etc/icg,
  /etc/icg/packs, /etc/icg/overrides and /var/cache/icg. No mode anywhere in
  the image's trust path may depend on the ambient umask.
- /etc/icg/packs is chmodded BEFORE the `COPY packs /etc/icg/packs/` line;
  verify the COPY does not relax it (the child-4 build assertion catches this
  either way, but state which of the two wins and why in a comment).
- The kaniko umask 0000 finding is recorded in a Dockerfile comment so the
  next reader does not "fix" the explicit modes back to bare mkdir.
- Change committed to main and pushed to Forgejo origin.
issue.notes:
Finished and shipped the partial diff left by the parent's failed attempts (irrevers-beee1069), containers/argo-guarded-builder/Dockerfile only.

What was already in the tree and verified rather than rewritten: (1) the mkdir RUN now chowns root:root and chmods 0755 /etc/icg /etc/icg/packs /etc/icg/overrides /var/cache/icg, so no trust-path mode depends on the build umask; (2) the kaniko umask-0000 finding is recorded as a Dockerfile comment citing the 0.1.0 evidence and irrevers-beee1069; (3) a build-time assertion RUN fails the image build if any of the four dirs is non-root-owned or world-writable; (4) the exact version check on icg --version was replaced by a semver-shape check -- verified necessary, Cargo.toml is 0.1.6 while ARG ICG_VERSION defaults to 0.1.0, so the old check failed every build.

What I added: the missing acceptance-criterion comment on ordering -- the chmod lands before 'COPY packs /etc/icg/packs/' and the chmod wins, because a COPY into an existing destination directory only adds entries and never re-modes it; imposing the source dir's mode happens only when the COPY creates the destination, which is exactly the 0.1.0 escape.

Verification: sanity-checked the assertion's world-writable case patterns against 755/555/750/777/1777/2755/40777 (catches the defect modes, passes 0755); no Rust test parses the Dockerfile and no operator doc makes a mode claim, so nothing else needed updating. The image itself was NOT built here -- builds run on kaniko in iad-ci at release time, and the assertion RUN is the in-build verification. VERSION (0.1.1, dirty) and the src/tests/docs edits belong to sibling beads and were left unstaged.

issue.close_reason: Implemented the Tier 1 git-commit-without-pathspec CommandRegex guard for -a/--all and message-only commits, with deny-only actionable redirects, quoted-token normalization, and hook/argv regression tests; committed as 720356f and pushed to origin/main.
issue.description:
CommandRegex, both front-ends, deny-only for v1 (Tier 1 -- stateless, decidable from a single invocation: the command text alone shows whether -a/--all is present, or whether trailing pathspec arguments exist after -m/--message). Denies git commit calls that would commit the entire staged index rather than an explicit path set: git commit -a/--all, and bare git commit -m "..." (or --message) with no trailing pathspec arguments.

This is a distinct gap from CLAUDE.md's existing git-staging rule. That rule already bans git add -A/git add ./git commit -a -- but an agent following it precisely (staging only explicit paths via git add <paths>) can still sweep unrelated pre-staged content into its commit if it then runs a bare git commit -m with no pathspec of its own, since git commit with no path arguments commits the full current index, not just what was just added.

Root incident (2026-08-14, commitgraph, worker claude-code-glm-5-adr018, bead cg-194i4a): git add containers/migration-worker/migrator.py containers/migration-worker/test_migrator.py (correct, precise staging) followed by bare git commit -m "..." produced commit 2bcbfe2, which also included ~430 unrelated lines from containers/queue-api/internal/{server,storage}/blocklist*.go -- pre-staged by a different concurrent NEEDLE worker in the same shared checkout. The worker self-corrected (git reset --soft HEAD~1 plus a clean re-commit passing the same two paths to git commit itself, landing as 1543ae2, verified never pushed to origin) before this rule existed to catch it mechanically -- this bead exists so the correction doesn't have to depend on a worker noticing on its own next time.

Distinct failure mode from Stale-HEAD push guard (irrevers-8cff8cf4): that catches pushing on top of remote state that's since moved. This catches unrelated staged content riding into a commit within the same shared tree, before any push ever happens -- the exact incident class that guard's own description already flags as outside its scope.

Redirect: deny + actionable reason ("pass the same file paths to git commit that you passed to git add -- git commit <paths> -m \"...\""). Not updatedInput: Tier 1 has no memory of what a prior git add in the same session actually staged (that is Tier 2 territory, per Architecture), so the correct pathspec to substitute is not derivable from the git commit call's own text -- per docs/notes/redirect-not-just-block.md, updatedInput is reserved for transformations that preserve intent through a derivable safer mechanism, which this is not. Stays deny with an actionable message, same tier/channel as its git-pack siblings (force-push detection, Stale-HEAD push guard).

Applies to all repos, not just known-shared-checkout ones (user direction 2026-08-14) -- explicit pathspecs on git commit have no real downside in an uncontended repo, so this is not scoped narrowly the way the beads-conjunction check is.

Plan: docs/plan/plan.md Phase 1 git pack -- also needs Architecture's pack list and Phase 1's rule-set prose updated to name this rule (not yet done as of this bead's creation).
issue.title: git pack: commit-without-pathspec guard

issue.close_reason: Fixed in 5546e48: --agent-user owns /var/cache/icg at 0700 and the installer verifies writability. Denial history confirmed written end to end.
issue.description:
`install.sh` created /var/cache/icg as root:root 0750, but the hook runs as
the agent identity (`coding` on ex44 and lab). The hook initializes its
telemetry store before evaluating, so every check emitted a permission
warning and — the part that matters — no denial history was ever written.

A practice-mode trial would have run for a week and produced nothing, which
is the entire output that trial exists for.

Fix: `--agent-user` (defaulting to SUDO_USER) owns the cache at 0700, and
the installer verifies that identity can actually write it rather than
trusting the chown.

The trust split is deliberate: the binary and /etc/icg stay root-owned so

issue.notes:
## Root Cause Identified

The pluck-query-debugger was filing false positive starvation alerts when the only bead in the system was an in-progress starvation-alert bead being actively worked on.

## The Bug

**Location:** `src/pluck_query_debugger.rs:804-833`

**Issue:** The `has_actionable_findings()` filter only excluded beads labeled `starvation-resolution` that were in_progress with an assignee. But starvation-alert beads (like this one) have different labels (`starvation-alert`, `alert:starvation:unknown`) and weren't filtered out, causing a circular false positive:

1. A starvation-alert bead is created (legitimately)
2. Agent claims it → status: in_progress, assignee: set
3. Pluck debugger runs: 1 in_progress bead, 0 ready frontier → starvation_detected = true
4. Filter doesn't catch it (wrong label check)
5. New starvation-resolution bead filed ❌

**Why the exclusion is legitimate:** When a bead is in_progress with an assignee, it's correctly excluded from the ready frontier by the status filter. The Pluck query only returns open, unassigned beads for claiming.

## The Fix

Changed the filter from checking specific labels to checking the actual condition that makes exclusion legitimate:

**Before (line 812-816):**
```rust
if analysis.labels.contains(&"starvation-resolution".to_string())
    && analysis.status == "in_progress"
    && analysis.assignee.is_some() {
    return false;
}
```

**After:**
```rust
// Skip ANY beads that are in_progress with an assignee
// (they're being worked on, so exclusion is legitimate)
if analysis.status == "in_progress" && analysis.assignee.is_some() {
    return false;
}
```

This prevents the false positive loop for ANY bead being worked on, not just specific labeled ones.

## Verification

- ✅ Fix applied to `src/pluck_query_debugger.rs`
- ✅ Build succeeds (cargo build --bin pluck-query-debugger)
- ✅ Pluck debugger detects starvation (expected) but does NOT file new bead (fixed)
- ✅ No new starvation-resolution beads created after fix
- ✅ Ready frontier correctly returns 0 beads (only in_progress bead exists, which is correct behavior)

The system now correctly distinguishes between:
- **Real starvation:** Open, unassigned beads exist but Pluck query excludes them due to bugs
- **False starvation:** Only in_progress beads exist (being worked on), so 0 ready frontier is correct

```rust
let starvation_detected = total_open_beads > 0 && ready_frontier_count == 0;
```

```rust
let starvation_detected = total_open_beads > 0 && ready_frontier_count == 0;
```

issue.description:
The operator-facing readout for a practice-mode trial cannot read the trial's
data, and fails in a way that names the wrong problem.

    $ icg status --denials --since 30d
    Error: invalid denial record in /var/cache/icg/session-state.json
    Caused by: EOF while parsing an object at line 1 column 1

## Root cause

`DenialLog::default_path()` (src/denial_log.rs:376) is
`/var/cache/icg/denials.jsonl`, with a comment explaining the choice --
/var/cache is writable by the hook identity, unlike /etc/icg. That is where
the hook writes.

`default_denial_log_paths()` (src/documented_commands.rs:1505), which the
reader uses, never consults it. It offers:

    /var/log/icg/denials.jsonl     <- does not exist
    /var/log/icg/denials.log       <- does not exist
    StateStore::default_path()     <- /var/cache/icg/session-state.json

The third is a *state* file, not a denial log. `operator_denial_path` picks
the first candidate that `is_file()`, so it selects the state file, then
`load_operator_denials` fails parsing it and reports "invalid denial record",
which reads like log corruption rather than the reader looking in the wrong
place.

Reader and writer each have a default and they disagree.

## Impact

Both hosts instrumented on 2026-09-06 (lab, ex44) are collecting practice
data that the documented command cannot read. That command appears in the
installer's completion notes, docs/quick-start.md, the training manual, and
irrevers-19835ba1's own acceptance criteria. Workaround today:

    ICG_DENIAL_LOG=/var/cache/icg/denials.jsonl icg status --denials --since 30d

`--pattern-summary` and `icg export-denial` take the same path and are
equally affected.

## Done when

- The reader's default comes from `DenialLog::default_path()`, so the two
  cannot drift apart again.
- The state-store path is not offered as a denial log.
- A candidate that exists but is not a denial log is skipped rather than
  selected, and the not-found error names the paths tried.
- `icg status --denials --pattern-summary` works on a stock install with no
  environment variables set.
issue.title: icg status --denials reads the wrong path and dies on the state file

issue.description:
## Alternative for: Starvation alert: beads invisible in 
Original bead: irrevers-76a2a7a7

Create a verification tool that compares three views of bead state: 1) SQLite database (`beads.db` via `bead list --json`), 2) Checkpoint files (`.beads/checkpoint/current.json` and `.beads/checkpoint/forensic.jsonl`), 3) Git-tracked checkpoint state. The tool would detect divergences like: a bead exists in the database but not in checkpoint, or vice versa. When divergence is found: 1) Run `bead sync flush-only` to force database->checkpoint sync, 2) If sync fails or shows errors, run `bead doctor --repair` for safe auto-repair, 3) For corruption beyond doctor's scope, rebuild from checkpoint using `bead init` + `bead sync import-only --input .beads/checkpoint/forensic.jsonl --restore-into-empty`. This prevents the scenario where workers read from a stale or corrupted view while the database has moved on.

---
This is an automated alternative proposal created by the unravel strand. It is a child of the original human-blocked bead and can be executed independently.
issue.notes:
Implemented bead database integrity checker at scripts/bead-integrity-check/. The tool compares three views of bead state:

1. **Database view**: SQLite database (beads.db) via direct SQL queries + bead list --json
2. **Checkpoint view**: current.json + forensic.jsonl (JSONL format) with nested issue objects
3. **Git view**: Checkpoint files from git HEAD using git2 crate

The tool detects divergences:
- database_ahead_of_checkpoint (HIGH): checkpoint stale, run 'bead sync flush-only'
- checkpoint_ahead_of_database (HIGH): database corruption, run 'bead doctor --repair' then rebuild
- git_ahead_of_checkpoint (MEDIUM): uncommitted changes, review and sync if needed
- stale_assignees (MEDIUM): open beads with assignees (reopen bug), clear assignees
- count_mismatch_* (LOW/MEDIUM): view count differences, sync recommended

Exit codes: 0 (no divergences), 1 (critical repair needed), 2 (non-critical review needed)

Output: Human-readable summary with emoji indicators + machine-readable JSON report.

Binary: /home/coding/target/release/bead-integrity-check or symlink at scripts/bead-integrity-check-bin

Verified against current workspace:
- Database: 168 beads ✅
- Checkpoint: 168 beads ✅
- Git: 146 beads (normal - uncommitted checkpoint changes)

Tested: Tool correctly identifies database/checkpoint sync and provides appropriate repair guidance.

Prevents starvation scenario where workers read from stale checkpoint while database has moved on (original bead irrevers-76a2a7a7 concern).

issue.close_reason: Hook mode now loads modular pack directories via --rule-pack or ICG_RULE_PACK, defaulting to /etc/icg/packs with legacy-file fallback; added production coverage and release/deployment artifact guidance.
issue.notes: Found while shipping the secrets pack (irrevers-ef9a4767). The engine supports unconditional packs (empty tool_keywords -> evaluate_unconditional_packs scans the whole command/content), and icg hook loads a single pack file via --rule-pack (default /etc/icg/rule-pack.json). But build-pack (src/rule_pack.rs, c2fcfd9) deliberately EXCLUDES unconditional packs from the merged artifact -- merging them would silently drop their whole-command coverage behind the union of tool_keywords (correct refusal; see the merge_packs mixed-merge error text). Net effect: a production hook pointed at the merged artifact gets NO secrets, image-tag, or storage-class coverage -- three shipped packs are unreachable in the documented deployment shape (docs/operators/deployment-guide.md installs exactly one merged /etc/icg/rule-pack.json). The c2fcfd9 error text already prescribes the mechanism: 'Distribute the packs directory as-is (ICG_RULE_PACK=/etc/icg/packs)' -- but nothing implements it: icg hook has no directory loading (load_pack is single-file; ICG_RULE_PACK is read only by src/monitoring.rs for status), and the Dockerfile/deployment guide install the single merged file. Fix direction: teach the hook path (and ideally icg update's artifact layout) to load every *.json in a directory when the configured path is a directory, then update the deployment guide + icg-ci release artifact accordingly. Verified 2026-08-25: build-pack output lists all three skipped; icg hook --rule-pack packs/secrets.json works single-pack (deny fires, [pack=secrets, pattern=github-token]).
issue.title: Hook mode cannot load unconditional packs (secrets, image-tag, storage-class) in production

The issue may stem from checkpoint desynchronization between `beads.db` and `.beads/checkpoint/`. Implement a tool that:

2. Parses the checkpoint files (`checkpoint/current.json`, `checkpoint/forensic.jsonl`, `checkpoint/objects/*.jsonl`)

This addresses checkpoint-related starvation issues without risking data loss from improper database rebuilds.

issue.description:
Implement a pure predicate function that determines whether a given path string refers to a location under .github/workflows/**. Handle path normalization: relative paths, absolute paths, paths with ./ segments, and OS-relevant case sensitivity.

Acceptance:
- Matches .github/workflows/** for relative, absolute, and ./-prefixed paths.
- Does not match paths that merely contain the substring 'workflows' outside of .github (e.g. src/workflows/foo.yml).
- Does not match sibling directories that look similar (e.g. .github/workflows-extra/foo.yml).
- Unit tests cover true positives and the false-positive fixtures above.
- No panics on malformed path strings (empty string, unusual encodings, etc).
- Parent bead: irrevers-e58ddf25.
issue.notes: Verified already implemented in commit e58cc4b (already on main, pushed, matches HEAD). src/github_workflows.rs::is_github_workflows_path is a pure predicate with lexical normalization (Path::components, handles ./, .., absolute, relative, repeated separators, trailing slash) and OS-appropriate case sensitivity via cfg!(windows/macos). 20 unit tests cover all acceptance criteria: relative/absolute/./-prefixed matches, substring false positives (src/workflows, .github/workflows-extra, .github/workflows2, .github/workflows-archive), empty string, and unusual encodings (NUL bytes, control chars, non-ASCII) with no panics. Ran 'cargo test --lib github_workflows' — all 20 pass. No changes made; nothing to commit.

The Problem:
- count_total_open_beads() counted beads with status IN (open, in_progress)

Implement the runtime behavior for both policy modes: fail-open (current baseline, guard crashes don't halt fleet) and fail-closed (fleet halts when guard is unhealthy).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Fail-open mode: Guard crashes log errors but fleet continues running (current behavior, now explicit)
- Fail-closed mode: Guard crash triggers immediate fleet halt via poison-pill
- Mode configurable via environment variable or config file
- Mode state persisted and recovered after restarts
- Integration with health tracking from bead irrevers-ffdc924b
- Unit tests for both modes
- Integration tests simulating guard crashes in both modes
- Designs from beads irrevers-aab3854c and irrevers-ffdc924b reviewed and followed

## Dependencies
Blocks: irrevers-019c36d3 (parent)
Blocked by: irrevers-ffdc924b (health tracking bead)

## Notes
This bead implements the actual runtime behavior change. The default MUST be fail-open to match current org-rule-guard.py philosophy. Fail-closed is opt-in.

issue.description: Before allowing git push, compare the local checkout's tracked remote HEAD against the actual current remote HEAD (live check); if they differ, fail the push and redirect the agent to pull and resolve first. Simpler revision of the original shared-tree-collision idea (cross-process /proc scanning), per user direction 2026-08-13. issue.description:
Split child of irrevers-92e6e55c; last in the chain -- closes the loop on the parent's remaining done-when items.

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] `icg policy status` and `icg policy reconcile` verified working as root on a normally-installed host layout -- record the result of the check only, never a policy value or credential.
- [ ] Locking now lives only in operator / deployment-controller commands (`icg policy reconcile`/`configure`/`demote`); confirm by grep that no guarded-path caller reaches `acquire_lock`, and note the evidence.
- [ ] The deployment guide's ownership table states explicitly that `/etc/icg/fail-closed-policy.json` and its `.lock` stay root-only, that guarded agents neither write nor lock them, and why the "agent-writable .lock" alternative was rejected (an agent must not hold a lock on state it cannot legitimately alter, and the subsequent policy write would fail anyway).
- [ ] The full fail_closed graduation suite passes unchanged (`cargo test`) -- the parent's third done-when item.
- [ ] Results recorded as a note on irrevers-92e6e55c.
issue.notes:
Verified by child bead irrevers-93baa29a, 2026-09-07.

Reproduction note for this host: bare `sudo` on codinghome resolves to the non-setuid nix-store path and fails with "sudo: /run/current-system/sw/bin/sudo must be owned by uid 0 and have the setuid bit set". The working setuid wrapper is /run/wrappers/bin/sudo, which is not on PATH. Every run below used `/run/wrappers/bin/sudo -n /usr/local/bin/icg ...`.

Installed host layout (/usr/local/bin/icg, root-owned /etc/icg, installed 2026-09-06):

1. `policy status` — exit 0, empty stderr. Bootstrapped state reported: Mode FailOpen, clean-release streak zero, no last poison-pill event, no last transition. The durable policy file does not exist on this host; status bootstraps in memory and writes nothing.
2. `policy reconcile` (live stores) — exit 0, empty stderr, outcome `Pending { reason: "no trusted release pointer exists" }`. The Pending path takes the exclusive policy lock but writes nothing (policy file still absent afterwards); a repeat run is idempotent with the same outcome. Documented reason the clean-release observation cannot advance on the live stores: this host has no trust pointer and no qualifying release evidence — that is Pending, not a failure.
3. Ownership check: live runs emitted no warning, while scratch-store runs (policy directory owned by uid 1000) emitted the documented "Custom artifact directory ... is owned by uid 1000, not root" warning — so the installed root-owned /etc/icg passes the directory-ownership check.

Both reconcile directions were exercised through the documented `-p` / `--state-store-path` / `--trust-pointer-path` overrides against throwaway scratch stores (same installed binary, as root, synthetic data only; live /etc/icg and /var/cache/icg never touched — re-verified after cleanup: live policy file absent, Mode FailOpen):

- Poison-pill direction, policy open: unprocessed rollback count in the scratch state store → exit 0, outcome `PoisonPill(PoisonPill { ... })`; durable event type PoisonPill recorded, qualification reset, mode stays FailOpen. Re-running reconcile consumes the event exactly once (subsequent run: `Pending`).
- Clean-release direction: trust pointer plus complete per-release telemetry (current release above the minimum observation count, prior-release baseline above the minimum evaluation count, non-concerning deviation) → exit 0, outcomes `Clean(CleanRelease { ... })`, `Clean(CleanRelease { ... })`, then `Clean(Graduated { ... })`: mode committed FailClosed at threshold. Re-running with the same release ref → `NoChange` (idempotent, as documented).
- Poison-pill direction, policy already FailClosed: new unprocessed rollback count → exit 0, outcome `PoisonPill(PoisonPill { ... })`; mode preserved as FailClosed and the event consumed — matches the documented "remain Fail-Closed" contract.

All status and reconcile invocations exited 0; live runs had empty stderr; nothing failed and nothing was papered over. No policy value, policy file content, or credential appears in this note or in any command line — only exit codes, outcome variants, transition/event names, and reason shapes.

---

Lock-ownership grep verification (child irrevers-10fa65df, 2026-09-08, code state main 08f5be4):

Criterion "no guarded-path caller reaches acquire_lock" FAILS for the fail-closed policy lock. One guarded-path chain reaches the lock, through crash recovery: `icg hook`, `icg wrapper`, and argv[0]-shadowed tool invocations all reach acquire_lock when a recovered guard crash is consumed. Filed as irrevers-3e6c6fde (defect; deliberately not fixed inside the child).

Evidence, all greps run from the repo root:

1. `grep -n acquire_lock src/fail_closed.rs` → 4 hits: 563 (private fn definition), 676 (in save), 685 (in update), 735 (in reconcile_release_health). Exactly the 3 call sites the criterion names.
2. `grep -rn acquire_lock src/ tests/ | cut -d: -f1 | sort | uniq -c` → fail_closed.rs 4, health.rs 6, state_store.rs 3. The fail-closed lock is named only inside fail_closed.rs, so every reach goes through a PolicyStore method (health/state-store locks are out of scope per the child).
3. `grep -rln PolicyStore src/ tests/` → src/fail_closed.rs, src/engine.rs, src/main.rs, plus tests/fail_closed_policy_tests.rs and tests/fail_closed_runtime_tests.rs. No other module can reach the store.
4. Read-only guarded loads confirmed: engine.rs:991-992 constructs `PolicyStore::from_env()` and calls `load()` only (no lock) for every evaluation path, and `icg policy status` (main.rs:2474-2477) is `store.load()` only.
5. Mutating entry points and what reaches them:
   - save (fail_closed.rs:676): zero production callers — only test seeding (tests/fail_closed_runtime_tests.rs:74,216,290). No subcommand reaches it.
   - update (fail_closed.rs:685) wrappers: record_clean_release has zero callers anywhere (dead public API); set_threshold / emergency_demote / force_graduate / force_revert are called only at main.rs:2532 / 2544 / 2552 / 2560, all inside Commands::Policy (icg policy configure / demote / force-graduate / force-revert); reconcile_release_health (fail_closed.rs:735) is called only at main.rs:2520 (icg policy reconcile). Those operator subcommands are clean.
   - THE DEFECT: main.rs:916 `policy_store.record_poison_pill(&event_ref)` sits in recovered_guard_crash_requires_halt (main.rs:906), called from main.rs:1177 inside run_shadowed_tool (reached from the argv[0]-shadowed tool path at main.rs:1370 and `icg wrapper` at main.rs:1807) and from main.rs:1627 inside Commands::Hook. Chain: icg hook / icg wrapper / shadowed tool → record_poison_pill (fail_closed.rs:696) → update (685) → acquire_lock (563).
6. `grep -n recovered_guard_crash_requires_halt src/main.rs` → 3 hits: definition 906, calls 1177 and 1627.
7. Impact splits by layout (detail on irrevers-3e6c6fde): on this host's hardened root-owned layout the hook's lock open fails permission-denied and the crash-recovery poison-pill event is silently dropped (stderr warning, main.rs:920-922) — tests/fail_closed_runtime_tests.rs:126 asserts the event persists and only passes because the test's policy path is agent-writable; on an agent-writable layout a guarded call instead takes the exclusive lock and writes policy state. Both contradict the acquire_lock doc comment (fail_closed.rs:557-562) and criterion 3's ownership table.

No source files changed for this verification; the defect is filed, not fixed, per the child's criterion 4.

issue.description:
Observed on lab immediately after the 2026-09-06 practice deployment.

Every hook invocation emits:

    ⚠️  Failed to reconcile fail-closed graduation policy
        /etc/icg/fail-closed-policy.json: failed to open fail-closed policy
        lock: Permission denied (os error 13)

`FailClosedPolicy::acquire_lock` (src/fail_closed.rs:557) opens the lock
with `create(true).write(true)` inside `$CONFIG_DIR`, which is root-owned by
design -- the deployment guide's ownership table lists
`/etc/icg/fail-closed-policy.json` as root:root, and the whole point is that
the guarded agent cannot rewrite its own policy.

So the hot path asks for a write lock it can never be granted, on every
call, for every agent. On lab that is 48 agents; on ex44 it would be 79.

## Why it matters more than it looks

The decision is unaffected -- the policy read fails and the guard stays
FailOpen, which is correct. The cost is noise: a warning on stderr for every
tool call, which is exactly the channel a real problem would announce itself
on. The telemetry and denial-log warnings that revealed the cache-ownership
bug this same day would have been invisible in that stream.

## Options, none taken yet

- Read the policy without a lock in the hook path, and require the lock only
  in `icg policy reconcile`/`configure`/`demote`, which an operator runs as
  root. Reconciliation on every guarded tool call is doing work the guard
  does not need.
- Or make only the .lock file agent-writable while the policy JSON stays
  root-owned -- smaller change, but it lets the agent hold a lock on state
  it cannot legitimately alter, and the subsequent write to the policy file
  would fail anyway.

The first looks correct; it is a change to availability-policy code, so it
deserves its own review rather than being folded into a deployment.

## Done when
- A hook invocation on a normally-installed host emits no warning on stderr
  when the policy file is root-owned and the guard is FailOpen.
- `icg policy status/reconcile` still work as root.
- The graduation behaviour covered by fail_closed tests is unchanged.
issue.notes:
2026-09-08: the two code children and the regression tests are LANDED in
0a5faa9 (pushed to Forgejo). The warning this bead is about is gone from the
source. This bead stays open on irrevers-8d1f79a7 (verify operator commands as
root, document the lock ownership model).

Verified live, negative control against the deployed v0.1.3 binary rather than
a stash (shared checkout carries other workers' edits): same 0555 policy
fixture, v0.1.3 emits the "failed to open fail-closed policy lock: Permission
denied" line, the new build emits nothing. Both allow. Neither creates .lock.

Option chosen: the first one this bead proposed -- read without a lock in the
guarded path, require the lock only in operator commands. The "agent-writable
.lock" alternative was rejected for the reason recorded here (an agent must
not hold a lock on state it cannot legitimately alter, and the subsequent
write would fail anyway); irrevers-8d1f79a7 owns writing that into the
deployment guide.

## Not fixed by this, and it matters for the done-when
The deployed hosts still run v0.1.3, so lab and ex44 keep emitting the warning
on every call until a release ships and is installed. The first done-when item
("a hook invocation on a normally-installed host emits no warning") is true of
the source, NOT yet of either instance.

## Second source of stderr noise on the same path
With the policy warning gone, a healthy guarded call still emits
`icg_health_event event=run_started run_id=...` -- routine lifecycle telemetry
on the fault channel, every call, every agent. Different cause, same cost.
Filed as irrevers-0aa08f4e. The new regression test filters those lines rather
than asserting empty stderr, and says so at the assertion.

## Diagnostic hazard removed while here
This suite's env_lock propagated mutex poisoning, so one failing assertion
reported as five failures -- which is how irrevers-1517a263's note came to
record "fails 5/5" for what was a single wrong test. It now recovers via
PoisonError::into_inner.

issue.description:
## Genesis Bead
Tied to plan: docs/plan/plan.md

## Overview
A guard for AI coding/automation agents (Claude Code and Codex CLI) that intercepts commands before execution and blocks or redirects irreversible operations, extending -- and eventually superseding most of -- the existing org-rule-guard.py PreToolUse hook. Two front-ends (a PATH-wrapper binary and native PreToolUse hook adapters) share one engine and a modular pack-per-tool rule set.

## Source of truth for scope
DO NOT read a bead-ID checklist here. Previous genesis bodies were retired precisely because their hardcoded ID lists went stale, and bead-rs cannot edit a description to repair one. The live blocker list IS the phase list:

    bead why --id <this-bead-id>      # every open bead blocking completion
    bead list --ready                 # what is actually startable right now

## Progress
- [ ] Phase 0 -- deploy path: icg-ci pipeline (DONE), trust pointer (DONE), self-updater (DONE, but see deferral 6), release-integrity Layers 1/2/4, release-cutting runbook, deploy-location decision
- [ ] Phase 1 -- Tier 1 rules, deny-only, both front-ends where applicable
- [ ] Phase 2 -- cross-invocation state (Tier 2)
- [ ] Phase 3 -- redirect-mechanism richness (updatedInput, additionalContext, value derivation)
- [ ] Phase 4 -- ideation run 1 finalists
- [ ] Phase 5 -- ideation run 2 finalists

## Deliberate deferrals and known-accepted gaps (the fallback role of this bead)
Recorded so a later reader does not re-litigate them. A four-round /plan-to-bead audit decided NOT to fix these:
1. STALE PROSE INSIDE BEAD DESCRIPTIONS. bead-rs cannot edit a description and its --notes field has no read path, so fixing a sentence means closing and recreating the bead. Not worth the churn for the following, all prose-only -- WHERE PROSE AND EDGES DISAGREE, TRUST THE EDGES:
   - ~7 open beads cite dead short-form icg-* IDs (provenance from before the bead-rs rehydration).
   - Two beads contain unresolvable positional placeholders left by a bf batch file: the Layer 2 review bead's 'bead @2' means the coverage-diff report bead, and the admin-dispatch bead's '@1' means the self-updater bead.
   - The wrapper additionalContext bead says 'no current bead depends on this specifically' -- the Codex-fallback bead now does.
   - The stale-HEAD push bead calls itself an exception to a 'no-I/O' engine constraint. The plan's constraint is zero-NETWORK-I/O; local filesystem reads were never exceptions. Do not generalize that wording to the beads pack's stat check.
   - The test-infrastructure bead's stated symptom ('cannot find module icg::coverage') is stale -- src/lib.rs is committed and exports it.
   - The commit-without-pathspec bead's closing line asks for plan.md prose that has since been written (Architecture pack list and the Phase 1 rule set both name the rule now).
   A PRIOR AUDIT ROUND ALSO CLAIMED the Codex compatibility-matrix bead misattributes its ideation run. That claim was WRONG and is not repeated here: the bead's provenance line uses the run-1 format and ideas-ledger.md places finalist #6 (gap round G4) in the first-run section, matching plan.md's Phase 4 listing. The bead is correct.
2. REDUNDANT EDGES. ~50 blocker edges are transitively implied by another edge on the same bead. Left as documentary; they inflate apparent fan-in for critical-path analysis.
3. VALUE-DERIVATION HELPERS keeps its plural title, matching plan.md's own component name, despite failing a strict single-task title test. The schema-and-loader bead likewise keeps a decide-and-implement shape, mitigated because the contentious half of that decision was split out to its own naming bead.
4. CRATES.IO as a secondary version-check signal is named in the plan but has no bead -- conditional on ever publishing the crate.
5. ORG-RULE-GUARD.PY RULES 1 AND 2 (.github/workflows, kind: Job/CronJob) are not excluded on principle but are not scheduled by any phase, so the realistic end state is a kubectl-only rump PLUS those two. Rule 4 (mutating kubectl) is excluded permanently. Rule 5 is only half-absorbed: Phase 1 takes the Bash channel, the Write/Edit half stays.
6. TWO PHASE 0 ARTIFACTS SHIPPED INTO AGENT-WRITABLE PATHS and their beads are closed as complete -- the self-updater closed while the deploy-location decision governing its path was still open. Rather than reopen completed work, the residual is tracked as its own migration bead. Phase 0 is load-bearing: per plan.md nothing in later phases is meaningfully tamper-resistant until the deploy-location and release-gating work lands.
7. TWO BEADS LOOK ALREADY SATISFIED by committed work (test-infrastructure setup, coverage-diff fixtures) but stay open: the fixtures encode both the schema SHAPE and the pattern NAMING that two separate decision beads are chartered to settle, and both now block them. Run the test suite and close them once those decisions land.
8. ONE LONG SERIALIZATION IS ACCEPTED, NOT OVERLOOKED: the engine's fail-open guarantee is gated on the regression-suite generator (because its own acceptance says the fixtures must be wired as Layer 1 cases), and it in turn gates all three front-end installs -- so a Phase 0 CI-tooling decision sits on the critical path of every deployable front-end. If that ordering ever hurts, the fix is to let the fail-open fixtures start as plain cargo tests and wire them into Layer 1 later.

## Investigation Complete

**Root Cause Identified:**
The Pluck query debugger was misclassifying the status filter exclusion as 'unknown'. When a bead with `base_status = 'in_progress'` was excluded from levels 0-3 (because those levels only query for `base_status = 'open'`) and became visible at level 4 (Raw), the code incorrectly reported it as 'Excluded by unknown filter' instead of 'Excluded by status filter'.

**Fix Applied:**
Updated `determine_exclusion_filter()` in `src/pluck_query_debugger.rs` to correctly identify beads that become visible at the Raw level due to status filter relaxation. The fix now properly distinguishes:
- Beads with `base_status = 'in_progress'`: 'Excluded by status filter: bead status is in_progress (only open beads appear in ready frontier)'
- Assigned open beads: 'Excluded by assignee filter'

**Verification:**
After the fix, the diagnostic system now correctly reports:
- `irrevers-9e968139` (in_progress): 'Excluded by status filter'
- `irrevers-ad2b2e51` (in_progress): 'Excluded by status filter'

**Behavior is Correct:**
This exclusion is legitimate - the Pluck query is designed to return only `open` beads that are ready to be claimed. Beads with `in_progress` status are already being worked on and should NOT appear in the ready frontier. The diagnostic system now correctly identifies this as the status filter, not as an unknown issue.

**Files Modified:**
- `src/pluck_query_debugger.rs`: Updated `determine_exclusion_filter()` function (lines 611-622) to handle Raw level visibility correctly

issue.close_reason: Fixed in 5546e48: message alternation accepts the re-quoted form. 35 -> 106 caught on the 20k corpus, 0 false positives, ReDoS clean, release-gate unchanged.
issue.description:
The engine re-quotes a command before matching, so a message containing
quotes becomes the shell escape `'\''`. The rule's message alternative
`'[^']*'` stops at the first inner quote and the anchored match fails, so
the rule silently declines to fire.

    rule sees: git commit -q -m '$(cat <<'\''EOF'\''\n...\n)'

Measured on 20,007 real agent commands: of 476 `git commit` invocations the
rule caught 35 and missed 200 that had no pathspec. What decided the outcome
was the message's formatting, not whether a pathspec was passed — and the
missed form is the house style for multi-line messages.

Fix: the message alternation accepts the re-quoted form,
`'[^']*'(?:\\''[^']*')*` and the double-quoted equivalent.

Result: 35 -> 106 caught, 0 false positives against the 152 commands that do
pass a pathspec. ReDoS clean, release-gate corpus unchanged.

The residual 129 misses are irrevers-e8359267 (the lexer truncates the
segment), not this rule.

issue.description:
## Genesis Bead
Tied to plan: docs/plan/plan.md

## Overview
A guard for AI coding/automation agents (Claude Code and Codex CLI) that intercepts commands before execution and blocks or redirects irreversible operations, extending -- and eventually superseding most of -- the existing org-rule-guard.py PreToolUse hook. Two front-ends (a PATH-wrapper binary and native PreToolUse hook adapters) share one engine and a modular pack-per-tool rule set.

## Source of truth for scope
DO NOT read a bead-ID checklist here. Three previous genesis bodies were retired because their hardcoded ID lists went stale, and bead-rs cannot edit a description to repair one. The live blocker list IS the phase list:

    bead why --id <this-bead-id>      # every open bead blocking completion
    bead list --ready                 # what is actually startable right now

This repo has a live NEEDLE worker in it. Beads close, split and get recreated continuously -- treat any narrative below as of its writing, and the edges as current.

## Progress
- [ ] Phase 0 -- deploy path: icg-ci pipeline (DONE), trust pointer (DONE), self-updater (DONE, see deferral 6), release-integrity Layers 1/2/4, release-cutting runbook, deploy-location decision
- [ ] Phase 1 -- Tier 1 rules, deny-only, both front-ends where applicable
- [ ] Phase 2 -- cross-invocation state (Tier 2)
- [ ] Phase 3 -- redirect-mechanism richness (updatedInput, additionalContext, value derivation)
- [ ] Phase 4 -- ideation run 1 finalists
- [ ] Phase 5 -- ideation run 2 finalists

## Deliberate deferrals and known-accepted gaps (the fallback role of this bead)
A five-round /plan-to-bead audit decided NOT to fix these. Recorded so a later reader does not re-litigate them:
1. STALE PROSE INSIDE BEAD DESCRIPTIONS. bead-rs cannot edit a description and its --notes field has no read path, so fixing a sentence means closing and recreating the bead. Not worth the churn for: ~6 open beads citing dead short-form icg-* IDs; two unresolvable positional placeholders left by a bf batch file (the Layer 2 review bead's 'bead @2' means the coverage-diff report bead, the admin-dispatch bead's '@1' means the self-updater bead); the wrapper additionalContext bead's claim that nothing depends on it (the Codex-fallback bead does); the stale-HEAD push bead calling itself an exception to a 'no-I/O' constraint when the plan's constraint is zero-NETWORK-I/O (local filesystem reads were never exceptions -- do not generalize that wording to the beads pack's stat check); and drifted plan.md line-number citations in several beads, which still name the right sections. WHERE PROSE AND EDGES DISAGREE, TRUST THE EDGES.
   An audit round claimed the Codex compatibility-matrix bead misattributes its ideation run. That claim was WRONG and is not repeated: the bead's provenance line uses the run-1 format and ideas-ledger.md places finalist #6 (gap round G4) in the first-run section, matching plan.md's Phase 4 listing.
2. REDUNDANT EDGES. ~55 blocker edges between live beads are transitively implied by another edge on the same bead. Left as documentary; they inflate apparent fan-in for critical-path analysis.
3. VALUE-DERIVATION HELPERS keeps its plural title, matching plan.md's own component name. The schema-and-loader bead likewise keeps a decide-and-implement shape, mitigated because the contentious half of that decision was split out and settled separately.
4. CRATES.IO as a secondary version-check signal is named in the plan but has no bead -- conditional on ever publishing the crate.
5. LAYER 3 (build provenance / signing) has no bead. plan.md Phase 0 explicitly defers it as later work alongside Layer 4's full form; only Layer 4's staged rollout got a bead. This is a deliberate plan-level deferral, not a coverage hole.
6. ORG-RULE-GUARD.PY RULES 1 AND 2 (.github/workflows, kind: Job/CronJob) are not excluded on principle but are not scheduled by any phase, so the realistic end state is a kubectl-only rump PLUS those two. Rule 4 (mutating kubectl) is excluded permanently. Rule 5 is only half-absorbed: Phase 1 takes the Bash channel, the Write/Edit half stays.
7. TWO PHASE 0 ARTIFACTS SHIPPED INTO AGENT-WRITABLE PATHS (/icg for the trust pointer, dirs::data_local_dir()/icg for the rule pack) and their beads are closed as complete -- the self-updater closed while the deploy-location decision governing its path was still open. Rather than reopen completed work, the residual is tracked as its own migration bead. Note that at the time of writing src/update.rs was still untracked in git despite its bead being closed, so verify what actually landed. Phase 0 is load-bearing: per plan.md nothing in later phases is meaningfully tamper-resistant until the deploy-location and release-gating work lands.
8. ONE LONG SERIALIZATION IS ACCEPTED, NOT OVERLOOKED: the engine's fail-open guarantee is gated on the regression-suite generator (its own acceptance says the fixtures must be wired as Layer 1 cases), and it in turn gates all three front-end installs -- so a Phase 0 CI-tooling decision sits on the critical path of every deployable front-end. If that ordering hurts, let the fail-open fixtures start as plain cargo tests and wire them into Layer 1 later.
9. RECREATING A BEAD DROPS ITS EDGES AND ITS BODY. This bit the graph twice during the audit: an in-flight terminology fix closed the two Layer 1 coverage-diff beads and recreated them with no description and no dependencies, orphaning them from the genesis and leaving two live beads blocked on the closed originals. If you close-and-recreate, rewire every dependent FIRST and copy the description -- bead-rs gives you no way to add one afterwards.

issue.notes:
Implemented comprehensive starvation diagnostic system with automated root cause analysis.

Implementation Complete: Created src/starvation_diagnostic.rs module and starvation-diagnostic binary that performs automated diagnostic when Pluck reports zero candidates despite open beads existing.

Five-Phase Diagnostic Suite:

1. Database State Analysis - Queries all open beads with full metadata (status, assignee, manual_blocked, priority, revision, dependencies)

2. Pluck Filter Replay - Replays the ready frontier filter logic (open + no assignee + not blocked) with detailed exclusion logging showing exactly why each bead is invisible: HasAssignee, ManualBlocked, WrongStatus

3. Checkpoint Sync Verification - Compares beads.db vs .beads/checkpoint/current.json: Detects missing, invalid, stale, or desynchronized checkpoints. Tracks checkpoint age and issue count differences. Configurable stale threshold (default 5 minutes)

4. Stale Assignee Detection - Identifies assigned-but-open failure mode: Checks each open bead with assignee, detects worker process status (active/inactive), flags beads needing assignee clearance

5. Database Integrity Verification - Validates: Database readability, Schema validity (issues table exists and queryable), Index validity (indexes working correctly), Corruption detection

Output: Structured JSONL reports at .beads/diagnostics/starvation-report.jsonl, Human-readable summaries with exclusion details, Recommended repair actions (checkpoint flush, assignee clears, etc.), Primary cause determination (stale_assignees_N, active_assignments_N, checkpoint_failure, etc.)

Usage: cargo run --bin starvation-diagnostic for normal operation, --json for JSON output, --report-only for no auto-repair

Test Results: All unit tests passing, Successfully detects open beads/exclusions/checkpoint staleness, Correctly identifies primary causes (active_assignments, checkpoint issues), Generates actionable repair recommendations

Exit Codes: 0 = No starvation detected or diagnostic completed successfully, 1 = Starvation detected (non-zero exit code for automation)

The diagnostic runs as an automated background task when starvation is detected—no human decision needed, just comprehensive analysis and actionable recommendations.

issue.description:
## Observed (plan-vs-built reference-integrity sweep, 2026-08-19)

`src/lib.rs` and `src/main.rs` declare modules whose files exist on this ex44
working tree but are NOT tracked by git. A fresh clone therefore cannot compile:
rustc fails on the first unresolved `mod`.

    src/lib.rs:4   mod alerting;      -> src/alerting.rs       746 lines  UNTRACKED
    src/lib.rs:7   mod denial_log;    -> src/denial_log.rs     916 lines  UNTRACKED
    src/lib.rs:9   mod health;        -> src/health.rs         905 lines  UNTRACKED
    src/lib.rs:10  mod health_server; -> src/health_server.rs  584 lines  UNTRACKED
    src/lib.rs:11  mod metrics;       -> src/metrics.rs        652 lines  UNTRACKED
    src/lib.rs:15  mod regex_safety;  -> src/regex_safety.rs   714 lines  UNTRACKED
    src/lib.rs:18  mod telemetry;     -> src/telemetry.rs      863 lines  UNTRACKED

5,380 lines in total. `src/lib.rs` declares 17 modules; only 13 `src/*.rs` files
are tracked. None of the seven is matched by .gitignore -- this is a plain
missing `git add`, not a deliberate exclusion.

This is the highest-severity form of the defect: the code passes every check on
the machine that wrote it, review never sees it, and deleting this working tree
destroys the only copy of all 5,380 lines.

## Do
Commit the seven files, naming each path explicitly -- never `git add -A`, which
on a shared checkout sweeps in whatever else is in the tree. Build first: if a
file does not compile it is in-flight work, so fix or exclude it deliberately
rather than committing a broken tree. If any module turns out to be genuinely
dead, delete its `mod` declaration instead -- but commit is the default, because
the declaration is what the tracked code already relies on.

## Done when
A clone from the remote resolves every module declaration and compiles:

    T=$(mktemp -d); git clone --quiet https://git.ardenone.com/jedarden/irreversible-command-gate.git "$T/r"
    cd "$T/r"
    grep -hoP '^\s*(?:pub\s+)?mod\s+\K\w+' src/lib.rs src/main.rs | sort -u | while read -r m; do
      [ -f "src/$m.rs" ] || [ -d "src/$m" ] || echo "UNRESOLVED $m"
    done
-> prints nothing

    cargo check --all-targets
-> exits 0
issue.title: Commit the seven src modules lib.rs declares but git does not track

issue.description:
Found by a new regression test failing in icg-ci run icg-ci-cc6b2 (2026-09-08).

Every hook invocation inside ronaldraygun/argo-guarded-builder:0.1.0 emits:

    🚨 POISON-PILL AUTO-ROLLBACK FAILED: Security violation: Artifact
    directory /etc/icg is world-writable (mode 40777). This allows any user
    to modify trust configuration. Run: sudo chmod o-w /etc/icg

The guard is right. `verify_artifact_directory_security`
(src/trust_pointer.rs:117) exists precisely to refuse a trust directory the
guarded process could rewrite, and in this image it can.

## Why this is worse than a noisy log line

This is the image the release pipeline builds and hands to other CI/build
pods -- "self-referential protection: the release workflow uses the same
guarded executor that it publishes" (icg-ci-workflowtemplate.yml). So the
guard is inert-by-trust-bypass in every guarded CI pod: anything running in
one of those containers can rewrite /etc/icg/trust-pointer.json and
/etc/icg/packs and thereby choose its own rules. That is the exact gap
docs describe org-rule-guard.py as having, and which this project exists to
close.

Note the failure mode: the check does not block. It reports and continues,
so the condition has been true on every guarded CI pod since the image was
built (2026-08-20) without anything going red.

## Cause, most likely

containers/argo-guarded-builder/Dockerfile:39 does

    RUN mkdir -p /etc/icg/packs /etc/icg/overrides /var/cache/icg

and never chmods them. Line 51 chmods /usr/local/bin/icg only. With a normal
umask mkdir yields 0755, so something in the base image or build environment
is applying a permissive umask -- worth confirming rather than assuming, then
setting the modes explicitly regardless. Do not rely on the ambient umask for
a directory whose whole purpose is being un-writable.

/etc/icg/packs, /etc/icg/overrides and /var/cache/icg need checking in the
same pass; only /etc/icg was named by the error.

## Done when
- /etc/icg and its subdirectories are explicitly chmodded in the Dockerfile,
  not left to umask
- a built image is inspected (stat, not the build log) and shows /etc/icg
  root-owned and not world-writable
- a hook invocation inside the image emits no security violation
- containers/argo-guarded-builder/VERSION bumped and the image published,
  then the icg-ci template pinned to it
- ideally the image build itself asserts the mode, so this cannot regress
  silently again
issue.notes:
2026-09-08: independently confirmed and refined by probe workflow
icg-beee1069-probe-l7zdq (Succeeded) against the shipped image.

## Modes as shipped (0.1.0)
    777 root /etc/icg
    755 root /etc/icg/packs        <- 755 only because COPY packs overwrote it
    777 root /etc/icg/overrides
    777 root /var/cache/icg
    755 root /usr/local/bin/icg

## Not a global umask
Same build's other directories are fine -- /var/lib/apt/lists 755,
/var/cache/apt 755, /usr/local/share 755 (/root/.cargo is 777, from the rust
base image). So the `RUN mkdir -p` at Dockerfile:39 is what produced 0777.
Set the modes explicitly there rather than chasing the umask.

## SECOND defect, and it outlives the chmod
Correcting /etc/icg to 0755 does NOT make the check pass in these pods:

    --- icg status (USER unset) ---  exit=1
    Security violation: Current user can WRITE to artifact directory /etc/icg.

The pods run uid=0 gid=0 with USER unset, and root can write a root-owned
0755 directory. With USER=root exported, the same command exits 0.

So the check keys off the USER *environment variable* rather than the real
uid. That is worth its own decision: an env var is not an identity, and a
guarded process can set it. Either the check should use the real uid (and
then decide deliberately what running-as-root means), or it should stop
consulting USER. Not fixed here -- it needs a decision, not a patch.

Consequence for the fix: chmodding the Dockerfile alone will NOT make the
guard quiet in CI. Both halves need addressing, or the pods need to run as a
non-root user.

Also observed: the binary embedded in 0.1.0 predates `icg policy`
("unrecognized subcommand 'policy'"), so the image is well behind source.

## Test side, already landed
tests/fail_closed_runtime_tests.rs skips the two policy tests when the
ambient trust directory fails this check, and as of 2e61ac4 it calls
verify_artifact_directory_security directly rather than testing the
world-writable bit -- so it stays correct through the chmod fix and only
starts running in CI once BOTH defects above are resolved.
issue.title: argo-guarded-builder ships /etc/icg world-writable, defeating the trust model in every CI pod
