issue.description:
## Alternative for: Starvation alert: beads invisible in 
Original bead: irrevers-b792cfe5

Implement automated repair that detects and fixes beads in the 'assigned-but-open' failure state: (1) Query all open beads with non-null assignees; (2) For each assigned open bead, check if the corresponding worker process is still active; (3) If the worker is no longer alive, automatically clear the assignee field, making the bead visible to the ready frontier; (4) Log each repair with timestamp, bead ID, previous assignee, and reason (worker deceased). This directly addresses the 2026-08-16 incident where 583 beads were starved across 47 workspaces due to stale assignees. The repair is deterministic: if a worker is dead, its assigned beads cannot be worked and must be released. No human decision required.

## Alternative for: Starvation alert: beads invisible in 
Original bead: irrevers-b792cfe5

Generalize the resolution: every starvation alert carries the `starvation-alert` label and has a mechanical verdict procedure, so none should sit in a human queue. (1) Enumerate workspaces from the NEEDLE workspace registry / active worker heartbeats; for each, detect the bead backend BEFORE running any bead command (`.beads/config.json` + `.needle.yaml` `bead_cli: backend: bead-rs` -> `bead`; `.beads/config.yaml` -> `bf`; ambiguous -> skip and log, never guess — the CLIs silently corrupt each other's schema). (3) For each hit, run `/home/coding/NEEDLE/scripts/starvation-triage.sh triage <id> --workspace <dir>`: false positives (0 open beads, payload contradicting prose) are closed with evidence; genuine starvation (actionable open+unassigned+unblocked beads) and inconclusive cases are NEVER closed — the script appends the per-bead actionable list to the alert's notes so dispatch can proceed without a human. (4) Run `starvation-triage.sh validate` first as a read-only gate; the 16 known coned-rate-optimizer false positives of 2026-08-27 are already classified and must be classification-validated only, never re-closed. Emit a per-bead verdict table (id, workspace, verdict, evidence) as the run's output artifact.

Evidence: 20,007 real agent commands replayed before and after. 71 newly denied, all classified as real bare git commits -- zero false positives introduced. 2 no longer denied, both false positives the fix REMOVED (a git commit inside a heredoc written to a file, and a docs edit mentioning bao kv destroy). Deny rate 0.205% -> 0.55%.

10 new tests in tests/heredoc_lexing_tests.rs, written failing first, covering both quote kinds, <<- tab stripping, an unterminated heredoc, a body containing the terminator as a substring, and the reverse direction (writing a destructive command into a file is still allowed).

547 tests pass; fmt and clippy clean; redos-check 0 unsafe of 30; release-gate corpus unchanged at 10 cases. Verified green end to end in icg-ci-k6nnf (Succeeded), which also proved the coverage-justification gate added in declarative-config 4951607b: 'Every flagged pattern has a recorded justification ... git-commit-without-pathspec' -> CI passed, where the identical change had failed icg-ci-9cwk7 outright.

Residual $( ) non-recursion split out as irrevers-3e313b79 and pinned by an #[ignore]d test.
issue.description:
## Symptom

A destructive command placed after a heredoc whose body contains an
apostrophe is ALLOWED:

    cat <<'EOF' > /tmp/note
    openssl-sys's build script
    EOF
    bao kv destroy secret/prod/db          -> allow

    cat <<'EOF' > /tmp/note
    it's a "test"
    EOF
    docker system prune --all --volumes    -> allow

Remove the apostrophe and both are correctly denied.

## Mechanism

`lex_shell_commands` (src/engine.rs:533) has no heredoc handling — there is
no `<<` case anywhere in engine.rs. Inside a `<<'WORD'` body the content is
literal shell text, but the lexer treats an apostrophe as opening a quote.
That quote never closes, the remainder of the command collapses into one
unterminated word, and no executable token is emitted after it.

Command-mode packs are dispatched by executable basename
(`Engine::get_executables` -> `segment_command`). With no `bao` token the
openbao pack is never consulted. Confirmed from the --debug trace: for the
first case above the dispatched packs were argocd-topology, image-tag,
secrets, storage-class — the four content/unconditional packs that scan the
raw string. openbao, git, docker, beads, misc and tmux were all skipped.

So this silently disables 6 of 10 packs, including every Critical
destructive rule.

## Scale

2.6% of real agent traffic hits the shape: 522 of 20,007 unique Bash
commands sampled from the last 1,500 agent transcripts on ex44 contain a
heredoc whose body has an apostrophe. This is ordinary English prose in a
file being written, not adversarial input.

Within the stated threat model (honest fallible agent) this is a coverage
hole rather than an exploit, but it fails open and silently, in exactly the
case the guard exists for.

## Also explains

The residual misses in `git-commit-without-pathspec`: the rule was handed a
segment truncated at 506 of 1357 characters. The regex fix in the same
commit raised the catch rate 35 -> 106 with zero false positives; the
remaining 129 are this bug.

## Done when

- The lexer consumes `<<WORD`, `<<'WORD'`, `<<"WORD"` and `<<-WORD` bodies
  literally up to the terminator, emitting no tokens from the body.
- All six cases in the symptom section deny.
- Regression tests cover: apostrophe in body, double quote in body, both,
  `<<-` with leading tabs, an unterminated heredoc, and a body that itself
  contains the terminator word as a substring.
- The 20k-command corpus replay shows no new false positives.
- `icg redos-check` and the release-gate corpus are unchanged.
issue.notes:
Fix implemented in f6aacc4 (committed, push held until ArgoCD syncs the
icg-ci gate change — pushing sooner would fail CI for the bookkeeping reason
in 4951607b).

## Acceptance evidence

Replayed all 20,007 real agent commands before and after:

              before            after
  allow       19,966 (99.80%)   19,897 (99.45%)
  deny            41 (0.205%)      110 (0.55%)

  newly denied:      71  — all classified: every one a real bare `git commit`.
                          Zero false positives introduced.
  no longer denied:   2  — both were FALSE POSITIVES the fix removed:
                          (a) `git commit` inside a heredoc written to a file
                          (b) an edit of deny-messages.md mentioning
                              `bao kv destroy`

So the fix adds 71 genuine catches and removes 2 false positives.

Note for irrevers-19835ba1: the 0.205% deny rate quoted in that bead was
measured with this bypass active and is an undercount. The real figure is
0.55%.

## Gates
- 547 tests pass (10 new in tests/heredoc_lexing_tests.rs, written failing first)
- cargo fmt --check and clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings clean
- icg redos-check: 0 unsafe of 30 patterns
- release-gate regression corpus unchanged at 10 cases
- coverage-diff flags the git regex change; justified in
  packs/coverage-justifications.md, which CI now reads (declarative-config
  4951607b)

## Not fixed here
irrevers-3e313b79 — the lexer does not recurse into $( ), so a commit message
containing a double quote truncates the segment. Verified to be neither a
bypass nor a false positive; pinned by an #[ignore]d test naming that bead.
issue.title: Lexer has no heredoc awareness: an apostrophe in a heredoc body disables every command-mode pack

issue.description:
Split child of irrevers-beee1069. Second, independent root cause of the
"Security violation: Artifact directory /etc/icg is world-writable" noise —
and the reason fixing the image modes alone is NOT enough.

src/trust_pointer.rs:176 gates the write probe on
`std::env::var("USER").as_deref() != Ok("root")`. In a container running as
root, USER is normally UNSET (nothing login-shaped sets it), so a root process
is treated as unprivileged, the write probe runs, succeeds — root can write
anywhere — and the check bails with a security violation even against a
correctly secured, root-owned 0755 /etc/icg. Every guarded CI pod runs as root
with no USER set, so this fires on every hook invocation regardless of the
directory's real mode.

Scope: src/trust_pointer.rs plus tests. NOTE: a partial diff using
libc::geteuid() already exists uncommitted in the working tree; review, verify
and finish it rather than restarting.

Acceptance criteria:
- Root is detected by effective uid (libc::geteuid() == 0), never by an env
  var; the write probe is skipped for root.
- Non-root behaviour is unchanged: the probe still runs for unprivileged users
  and still bails when they can write the directory.
- Tests cover: root euid with USER unset (the CI pod case — no violation),
  root euid with USER=root, and non-root with and without write access.
- cargo fmt / clippy / test clean (cargo test on this box submits to iad-ci;
  commit first so it does not fall back to a local run).
- Change committed to main and pushed to Forgejo origin.
issue.title: Fix root detection in verify_artifact_directory_security to use geteuid, not the USER env var

- [ ] A missing policy file still yields the FailOpen bootstrap state with a zero streak.
- [ ] Mutating paths (`update`, `reconcile_release_health`, any other writer) keep taking the exclusive lock; their existing unit tests still pass.
- [ ] `cargo test` green for the fail_closed unit tests.

issue.description:
The rule matches every Write/Edit under `.beads/**`. The hazard it exists for
is corrupting the shared bead STORE. Those are not the same set, and the live
practice trial on lab showed the difference costs real work.

## Evidence

23 hits in ~21 hours on lab, all from one repo, none touching the store:

    6  /home/coding/domain-check/.beads/state/domchk-884dd8ae/render_markdown.py
    5  /home/coding/domain-check/.beads/logs/bf-6d3d6-classification.json
    3  /home/coding/domain-check/.beads/state/domchk-1835a393/sampler.sh
    3  /home/coding/domain-check/.beads/state/domchk-ca6412a0/compute_unique_commits_authors.py
    2  /home/coding/domain-check/.beads/state/domchk-990ef135/extract_traces.py
    1  each: extract_commits.py, compute_divergence_metrics.py,
            compile_report.py, bf-6d3d6-root-cause.json

Agents use `.beads/state/<bead-id>/` as per-bead scratch space. It is
gitignored (`.gitignore:66`), has 0 tracked files, and is not a bead-rs
directory -- bead-rs creates beads.db, checkpoint/, config.json,
diagnostics/, receipts/, traces/. `.beads/state/` and `.beads/logs/` are an
agent convention, and domain-check's .beads/ is full of similar ad-hoc files,
so this is established practice there rather than one worker misbehaving.

Six hits landed in a 25-minute window, which is an agent retrying against a
wall. Under enforcement all 23 would have been blocked, and the redirect it
would have shown -- "use `git worktree add --detach <dir> origin/main` for
.beads/ work" -- is nonsense advice for a throwaway script.

## Why the offline replay missed it

The 20,007-command corpus produced zero false positives, but never exercised
this rule: it sampled command-mode Bash calls, and this is a content-mode
Write/Edit rule scoped by `applies_to`. A point-in-time replay cannot stand
in for watching a fleet.

## Proposed scope

`is_shared_beads_target` (src/engine.rs:463) currently returns true for any
path under `<repo>/.beads` when `<repo>/.git` is a directory. Narrow it to
the files whose corruption the rule is actually about:

    .beads/beads.db  (and -shm, -wal, .lock)
    .beads/checkpoint/**
    .beads/*.jsonl          (issues.jsonl, events.jsonl, heartbeats.jsonl)
    .beads/config.json  .beads/config.yaml

and explicitly NOT `.beads/state/**`, `.beads/logs/**`,
`.beads/diagnostics/**`, `.beads/traces/**`, `.beads/receipts/**`,
`.beads/crash-reports/**`, or loose scratch files.

Open question for the operator, recorded rather than assumed: should
`.beads/` scratch use be discouraged in its own right? If so that is a
convention change and a different rule, not a widening of this one -- this
rule's message and severity (Critical) are about store corruption.

## Done when
- Writing `.beads/state/<id>/foo.py` in a shared checkout allows.
- Writing `.beads/beads.db` or `.beads/checkpoint/current.json` still denies.
- Regression tests cover both directions plus a linked worktree (.git as a
  file), which must continue to allow.
- Re-run against lab's recorded paths: all 23 become allows.
issue.title: beads-shared-checkout-write fires on scratch files, not the bead store

## Overview
Connect the fail-closed transition to the existing poison-pill auto-rollback mechanism (icg-2ck) to automatically detect maturity and graduate from fail-open to fail-closed after N consecutive clean releases.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Integration with existing poison-pill deny-rate tracking
- Graduation trigger logic: N consecutive releases with zero poison-pill triggers
- Graduation threshold configurable (default TBD at implementation)
- Automatic state transition: Fail-Open → Fail-Closed when threshold reached
- Graduation event logged and telemetered
- Manual override capability (force graduate, force revert)
- Integration tests for graduation logic
- Designs from beads irrevers-aab3854c, irrevers-ffdc924b, irrevers-8a24ad8d reviewed and followed

## Dependencies
Blocks: irrevers-019c36d3 (parent)
Blocked by: irrevers-8a24ad8d (implementation bead)

## Notes
This leverages existing poison-pill tracking rather than inventing a new maturity signal. The integration must be read-only for poison-pill data - no modifications to icg-2ck behavior.

Deploy location decision clarified in plan.md

Decided that guard artifacts should be deployed to root-owned system paths:
- Binary: /usr/local/bin/icg (root:root, 0755)
- Rule packs: /etc/icg/packs/ directory (root:root, 0755) with individual pack files (root:root, 0644) - MODULAR approach preferred
- Trust pointer: /etc/icg/trust-pointer.json (root:root, 0644)

The modular pack-per-tool design (/etc/icg/packs/) is the recommended deployment shape, matching the architecture principle of 'not a monolithic rule list'. A legacy single-file /etc/icg/rule-pack.json is supported for compatibility but is not recommended.

This placement ensures the guarded agent's own process (running as 'coding') cannot write any of the three artifacts, fulfilling deployment shape 2 from runtime-config-vs-hardcoded.md. Updates require privilege escalation (sudo icg update).

5. Outputs detailed breakdown: per-bead exclusion reason, affected beads, suggested fixes

  cargo run --bin pluck-query-debugger -- --summary

Report written to .beads/diagnostics/pluck-query-debug-report.jsonl containing:

- Per-bead exclusion analysis (visible_at_level, excluded_by_filter, exclusion_reason)
- Exclusion patterns with matching bead IDs
- Recommended fixes if systematic patterns detected

detail.title: Routine run_started lifecycle telemetry prints to stderr on every guarded invocation

detail.reason:
Landed in 0a5faa9 (pushed to Forgejo).

PolicyStore::load was ALREADY lock-free at HEAD -- the criterion was met by
the code and undocumented, which is how the hook path came to reconcile on
every call without anyone noticing the read/write split existed. What this
adds is the contract, stated on both load() and acquire_lock(), so the next
caller cannot re-merge them silently. acquire_lock has exactly three callers,
all writers: save, update, reconcile_release_health.

Acceptance:
- read path performs no create/write open of .lock and no write under
  $CONFIG_DIR -- verified live, not by inspection: policy dir at 0555, the
  build emits nothing on stderr and no .lock appears (deployed v0.1.3 against
  the identical fixture emits the Permission denied warning)
- unwritable policy dir degrades silently to the bootstrap FailOpen state
- missing policy file yields FailOpen with a zero streak (unchanged)
- mutating paths keep the exclusive lock; their tests pass unchanged
- cargo test green: 216 unit + every integration suite; clippy -D warnings clean

Scope note for irrevers-8d1f79a7: one guarded-path caller still reaches a
writer -- recovered_guard_crash_requires_halt (src/main.rs:915) calls
record_poison_pill -> update -> acquire_lock. Left deliberately: it fires only
after an actual recovered guard crash, so on a root-owned policy dir it warns
in proportion to a real fault. The "no guarded caller reaches acquire_lock"
grep in that bead should expect and account for this one rather than treat it
as a miss.

Landed in 0a5faa9 (pushed to Forgejo).

reconcile_fail_closed_policy is deleted, not merely unwired -- both call sites
(the hook front-end at the former src/main.rs:835 and the guarded wrapper at
the former :1220) are gone, along with the function and the now-unused
PolicyTransition/ReconcileOutcome imports. Nothing can call it back by
accident.

Acceptance:
- neither front-end runs reconciliation or any other policy write on a
  guarded invocation
- both sites carry a comment naming `icg policy reconcile` as the operator
  action that owns graduation, and why the guarded process must not reconcile
- a guarded call against a root-owned (0555) policy directory emits nothing
  about the fail-closed policy on stderr, and the decision is unchanged:
  deployed v0.1.3 and this build both return permissionDecision allow on the
  same fixture; only v0.1.3 warns

`icg policy reconcile` still works and is covered by
operator_policy_commands_manage_the_durable_policy.

Landed in 0a5faa9 (pushed to Forgejo).

Two tests in tests/fail_closed_runtime_tests.rs:
- hook_invocation_leaves_administrator_owned_policy_untouched: policy dir at
  0555, asserts the decision is unchanged, the deployed state is untouched
  (mode preserved, no policy events written), no .lock is created, and stderr
  carries no fail-closed policy warning.
- operator_policy_commands_manage_the_durable_policy: proves locking was not
  deleted everywhere -- `icg policy status` and `icg policy reconcile` still
  read and mutate the durable store when it is writable.

## Which way it was checked
Negative control against a REAL unfixed binary, not a stash: /usr/local/bin/icg
(the deployed v0.1.3) and the working-tree build, same 0555 policy fixture,
same input. v0.1.3 emits "Failed to reconcile fail-closed graduation policy
... failed to open fail-closed policy lock: Permission denied (os error 13)"
-- which is what the assertion rejects. The new build emits nothing. Both
allow; neither creates the lock. Chosen over `git stash` because this is a
shared checkout carrying other workers' edits.

## Two defects in the in-flight test, both fixed
- it seeded via PolicyStore::save, which legitimately takes the lock, then
  asserted the hook had not created the lock its own setup had just made
- it matched "Mode: FailOpen" against markdown output reading "**Mode:** FailOpen"

## Harness fix worth knowing about
env_lock no longer propagates mutex poisoning (PoisonError::into_inner). The
guarded value is (), so a panic leaves nothing inconsistent, while propagating
it converted ONE real assertion failure into five. That is not hypothetical:
irrevers-1517a263's note recorded this suite as "fails 5/5", which read as
broad breakage when a single test was wrong.

## Deliberate weakening, tracked
The stderr assertion filters `icg_health_event ` lines instead of requiring
empty stderr: run_started telemetry prints on every guarded call for a
different reason (irrevers-0aa08f4e). The filter is a line-shape allow-list,
not a substring match, so any NEW warning still fails. Delete it and restore
stderr.is_empty() when that bead lands.

cargo test green: 216 unit + every integration suite; clippy -D warnings clean.

Landed in c6dcc3c (pushed to Forgejo).

Decided the first option: dropped the print, not gated behind a debug flag.
The bead said to prefer the gate only if something demonstrably reads these
lines -- checked, nothing does. No doc, script, monitor or test in the repo,
and nothing on either instrumented host, consumes icg_health_event output. The
run id is persisted in the health state immediately above the print and is
readable with `icg health`, so nothing is lost but the narration. A flag
nobody would set is surface, not a diagnostic.

Acceptance:
- a guarded hook invocation on a healthy host emits nothing on stderr --
  verified live against the real root-owned /etc/icg as the fleet runs it:
  zero bytes, decision unchanged (allow). Deployed v0.1.3 emits two lines on
  identical input.
- fault and crash-recovery events still print, proven by
  a_recovered_crash_still_announces_itself_on_stderr, which asserts
  crash_detected is present AND run_started is absent. crash_recorded and the
  *_failed variants are untouched.
- the filter in hook_invocation_leaves_administrator_owned_policy_untouched is
  deleted and the assertion is stderr.is_empty() again.

cargo test green (60 suites); clippy -D warnings clean.

Note for whoever ships the release: this and irrevers-92e6e55c's chain are
both source-only until a release is cut and installed. lab and ex44 keep
emitting both lines on every call until then.
